questions.explain: Rojo means red. A red apple is una manzana roja.
questions.tip: Rojo rhymes with 'oh no' - oh no, my red balloon popped!

questions.explain: Azul means blue, like the sky.
questions.tip: Azul sounds like 'a pool' - a big blue pool!

questions.explain: Verde means green, like grass.
questions.tip: Verde sounds a bit like 'very' - the grass is very green!

questions.explain: Amarillo means yellow, like the sun.
questions.tip: Amarillo sounds like 'armadillo' - picture a yellow armadillo!

questions.q: How do you say orange (the color) in Spanish?
questions.say: How do you say the color orange in Spanish?
questions.explain: Anaranjado means orange. Many people also say naranja.
questions.tip: Anaranjado has 'naranja' inside, and a naranja is an orange you can eat!

questions.explain: Blanco means white, like snow.
questions.tip: Blanco sounds like 'blank' - a blank page is white!

questions.explain: Negro means black, like the night sky.
questions.tip: Negro, negro, dark as night - turn off the lamp, no more light!

questions.explain: Morado means purple, like grapes.
questions.tip: Morado - more purple grapes, please!

questions.explain: Tres means three: uno, dos, tres.
questions.tip: Tres sounds like 'trace' - trace a triangle with 3 sides!

questions.q: How do you say two in Spanish?
questions.say: How do you say two in Spanish?
questions.explain: Dos means two.
questions.tip: Dos rhymes with 'close' - hold two hands close!

questions.explain: Cinco means five. You have cinco fingers on one hand.
questions.tip: Cinco sounds like 'sink-o' - wash your five fingers in the sink!

questions.explain: Diez means ten. You have diez fingers in all.
questions.tip: Diez sounds like 'dee-ess' - say yes to all ten fingers!

questions.explain: Uno means one.
questions.tip: Uno is the card game where you want just one card left!

questions.q: How do you say four in Spanish?
questions.say: How do you say four in Spanish?
questions.explain: Cuatro means four.
questions.tip: Cuatro sounds like 'quad' - a quad bike has four wheels!

questions.explain: Siete means seven.
questions.tip: Siete sounds like 'see-eh-tay' - see seven stars!

questions.explain: Ocho means eight. A spider has ocho legs.
questions.tip: Ocho starts with O, and an 8 is two O's stacked up!

questions.explain: Perro means dog. Woof!
questions.tip: Perro has a rolling r like a dog growling: grrr, perro!

questions.explain: Gato means cat. Meow!
questions.tip: Gato sounds like 'got-o' - the cat got your toes!

questions.explain: Pájaro means bird. Birds can fly.
questions.tip: Pájaro sounds like 'pa-ha-ro' - ha ha, the bird is laughing!

questions.explain: Pez means fish. A fish swims in water.
questions.tip: Pez is short and quick, just like a little fish!

questions.explain: Vaca means cow. Moo!
questions.tip: Vaca sounds like 'vacation' - the cow is on vacation in the field!

questions.explain: Caballo means horse. You can ride a caballo.
questions.tip: Caballo sounds like 'cab-eye-yo' - a horse is a cab you can ride!

questions.explain: Pato means duck. Quack!
questions.tip: Pato sounds like 'pat-o' - pat the duck's soft feathers!

questions.explain: Oso means bear. A teddy bear is un osito.
questions.tip: Oso sounds like 'oh so' - oh so big is the bear!

questions.explain: Hola means hello. You say it when you meet someone.
questions.tip: In hola the h is silent - just wave and say OH-la!

questions.explain: Adiós means goodbye. You say it when you leave.
questions.tip: Adiós: wave your hand and sing ah-dee-OHS!

questions.explain: Gracias means thank you.
questions.tip: Gracias sounds like 'grah-see-ahs' - say it with a big smile!

questions.explain: Por favor means please. It is a polite word.
questions.tip: Por favor has 'favor' inside - asking a favor needs a please!

questions.explain: Mamá means mom.
questions.tip: Mamá sounds just like mama!

questions.explain: Papá means dad.
questions.tip: Papá sounds just like papa!

questions.explain: Abuela means grandma. Grandpa is abuelo.
questions.tip: Abuela ends in a for grandma, abuelo ends in o for grandpa!

questions.explain: Hermano means brother. Sister is hermana.
questions.tip: Hermano ends in o for a brother, hermana ends in a for a sister!

questions.explain: In Spanish, once means eleven. It is not the English word once.
questions.tip: Once looks like an English word, but it means 11 - two ones standing side by side!

questions.explain: Doce means twelve. A dozen eggs is una docena.
questions.tip: Doce sounds like 'dozen' - a dozen is 12!

questions.explain: Quince means fifteen.
questions.tip: A quinceañera is a big party when a girl turns quince - 15!

questions.explain: Veinte means twenty.
questions.tip: Count 10 fingers and 10 toes and you get veinte!

questions.q: How do you say 16 in Spanish?
questions.say: How do you say sixteen in Spanish?
questions.explain: Dieciséis is sixteen. It means ten and six.
questions.tip: Dieciséis is diez y seis squished together: ten and six!

questions.explain: Ten plus ten is twenty, which is veinte.
questions.tip: Ten and ten: diez and diez make veinte!

questions.explain: Catorce means fourteen.
questions.tip: Catorce starts with 'cat' - picture 14 cats!

questions.q: How do you say 18 in Spanish?
questions.say: How do you say eighteen in Spanish?
questions.explain: Dieciocho is eighteen: ten and eight.
questions.tip: Dieciocho is diez y ocho squished together: ten and eight!

questions.explain: Trece means thirteen.
questions.tip: Trece starts like tres - 3 plus 10!

questions.explain: Lunes means Monday.
questions.tip: Lunes comes from luna (moon) - Monday is Moon-day!

questions.explain: Martes means Tuesday.
questions.tip: Martes is named after Mars, the red planet!

questions.explain: Miércoles means Wednesday.
questions.tip: Miércoles is named after Mercury, the speedy planet in the middle of the week!

questions.explain: Jueves means Thursday.
questions.tip: Jueves is named after Jupiter, the biggest planet!

questions.explain: Viernes means Friday.
questions.tip: Viernes is named after Venus - Friday is a shiny, happy day!

questions.explain: Sábado means Saturday.
questions.tip: Sábado and Saturday both start with S-a!

questions.explain: Domingo means Sunday.
questions.tip: Domingo is the last day of the Spanish week - Sunday fun day!

questions.explain: After lunes (Monday) comes martes (Tuesday).
questions.tip: Lunes then martes: the Moon, then Mars - the week zooms through the stars!

questions.q: In Spanish, the days of the week start with a capital letter.
questions.explain: False. In Spanish, days are written in small letters, like lunes, unless they start a sentence.
questions.tip: Spanish days are humble - no capital letters!

questions.explain: Manzana means apple.
questions.tip: Manzana sounds like 'man-sana' - a man eating a healthy apple!

questions.explain: Leche means milk.
questions.tip: Leche: a latte is coffee with lots of leche!

questions.explain: Pan means bread. It is not a cooking pan.
questions.tip: Pan is bread you could toast in a pan!

questions.explain: Agua means water.
questions.tip: Agua sounds like 'aqua' - the blue-green color of water!

questions.explain: Queso means cheese.
questions.tip: Queso is the cheese in a quesadilla!

questions.explain: Huevo means egg.
questions.tip: Huevo sounds like 'way-vo' - which way did the egg roll?

questions.explain: Pollo means chicken, the food.
questions.tip: Pollo sounds like 'POY-yo' - yo, chicken for dinner!

questions.explain: Arroz means rice.
questions.tip: Arroz con pollo: the arroz is the rice!

questions.explain: Cabeza means head.
questions.tip: Put a cap on your cabeza!

questions.explain: Mano means hand.
questions.tip: Mano is like 'manual' - something done by hand!

questions.explain: Pie means foot. It is not a pie you eat.
questions.tip: Pie is like 'pedal' - you push pedals with your feet!

questions.explain: Ojo means eye. You see with your ojos.
questions.tip: Ojo looks like a face: two O's for eyes and a j for a nose!

questions.explain: Nariz means nose. You smell with your nariz.
questions.tip: Nariz and nose both start with N!

questions.explain: Boca means mouth.
questions.tip: Open your mouth wide and say BO-ca!

questions.explain: Oreja means ear. You hear with your orejas.
questions.tip: Oreja sounds like 'oh, ray-ha' - oh Ray, can you hear me?

questions.explain: Brazo means arm. Leg is pierna.
questions.tip: Brazo sounds like 'bracelet' - a bracelet goes on your arm!

questions.explain: Libro means book.
questions.tip: Libro sounds like 'library' - a library is full of books!

questions.explain: Lápiz means pencil.
questions.tip: Lápiz sounds like 'lap-ease' - a pencil resting on your lap!

questions.explain: Maestra means teacher (a woman). A man teacher is el maestro.
questions.tip: Maestra sounds like 'maestro' - a master who teaches!

questions.explain: Silla means chair.
questions.tip: Silla sounds like 'see-ya' - see ya, I'm sitting in my chair!

questions.explain: Mesa means table.
questions.tip: Mesa sounds like 'mess' - don't make a mess on the table!

questions.explain: Escuela means school.
questions.tip: Escuela sounds like 'es-SCHOOL-a'!

questions.explain: Mochila means backpack.
questions.tip: Mochila: mo' stuff goes in my backpack!

questions.explain: Papel means paper.
questions.tip: Papel and paper both start with P-A-P!

questions.explain: ¿Cómo estás? means How are you?
questions.tip: Estás comes from estar, the feeling verb - how are you feeling?

questions.q: What does Me llamo Ana mean?
questions.say: What does me llamo Ana mean?
questions.explain: Me llamo Ana means My name is Ana.
questions.tip: Me llamo sounds like 'may YAH-mo' - picture a llama saying its name!

questions.say: What does cómo te llamas mean?
questions.explain: ¿Cómo te llamas? means What is your name?
questions.tip: Te llamas: what do they call you, little llama?

questions.explain: Bien, gracias means Fine, thanks. It answers ¿Cómo estás?
questions.tip: Bien sounds like 'be-en' - be fine, be happy!

questions.explain: Buenos días means good morning.
questions.tip: Días sounds like 'day-us' - good day to us!

questions.explain: Buenas noches means good evening or good night.
questions.tip: Noches sounds like 'nachos' - eating nachos at night!

questions.q: Someone says gracias. What do you say back?
questions.say: Someone says gracias. What do you say back?
questions.explain: De nada means you're welcome.
questions.tip: Nada means nothing - de nada, it was nothing!

questions.explain: Mucho gusto means nice to meet you.
questions.tip: Gusto means joy - it's a joy to meet you!

questions.explain: Hasta luego means see you later.
questions.tip: Luego sounds like 'Lego' - see you later, after we play Legos!

questions.explain: Treinta means thirty.
questions.tip: Treinta starts like tres - 3 tens make treinta!

questions.explain: Cincuenta means fifty.
questions.tip: Cincuenta starts like cinco - 5 tens make cincuenta!

questions.q: How do you say 100 in Spanish?
questions.explain: Cien means one hundred. Mil is one thousand.
questions.tip: Cien sounds like 'cent' - 100 cents make a dollar!

questions.explain: Veintiuno is twenty-one. Numbers 21 to 29 are written as one word.
questions.tip: Veinti plus uno glued together: twenty-one!

questions.q: What number is cuarenta y dos?
questions.explain: Cuarenta y dos means forty-two: forty and two.
questions.tip: Cuarenta starts like cuatro - 4 tens, and then y dos!

questions.explain: Setenta is seventy. Sesenta is sixty, so listen carefully.
questions.tip: Setenta starts like siete (7); sesenta starts like seis (6)!

questions.explain: Sesenta is sixty.
questions.tip: Sesenta starts with S-E like seis: six tens!

questions.q: How do you say 35 in Spanish?
questions.explain: Treinta y cinco is 35. Cincuenta y tres would be 53.
questions.tip: Y means and: treinta and cinco!

questions.explain: Noventa means ninety.
questions.tip: Noventa starts with N like nueve: nine tens!

questions.q: What number is ochenta y ocho?
questions.explain: Ochenta is 80, and ochenta y ocho is 88.
questions.tip: Ochenta starts like ocho - 8 tens, and then ocho more!

questions.explain: Enero is January, the first month.
questions.tip: Enero rhymes with hero - the hero month that comes first!

questions.explain: Julio is July.
questions.tip: Julio: hot July!

questions.explain: Junio is June.
questions.tip: Junio: think June-io!

questions.q: How do you say December in Spanish?
questions.explain: Diciembre is December.
questions.tip: Septiembre to diciembre end in -bre, just like English months end in -ber!

questions.explain: Agosto is August.
questions.tip: Agosto: a gust of hot August wind!

questions.explain: Marzo (March) is followed by abril (April).
questions.tip: Marzo, abril, mayo - March, April, May, same order!

questions.explain: Mayo is May.
questions.tip: Mayo: mayonnaise on a May picnic!

questions.q: In Spanish, the names of months are usually written with small letters, like enero.
questions.explain: True. Spanish months are not capitalized unless they begin a sentence.
questions.tip: Months are humble like days - no capital letters!

questions.explain: Hace calor means it is hot.
questions.tip: Calor sounds like 'calorie' - burning calories makes you hot!

questions.explain: Hace frío means it is cold.
questions.tip: Frío sounds like 'freeze-o' - brrr!

questions.explain: Está lloviendo means it is raining. You can also say Llueve.
questions.tip: The double L in lloviendo drips like raindrops!

questions.explain: Nieva means it is snowing. Snow is la nieve.
questions.tip: Nieva sounds like Nevada, a name that means snowy!

questions.explain: Hace sol means it is sunny. El sol is the sun.
questions.tip: Sol is like 'solar' - solar power comes from the sun!

questions.explain: Hace viento means it is windy.
questions.tip: Viento sounds like 'vent' - wind blows out of a vent!

questions.explain: Está nublado means it is cloudy. A cloud is una nube.
questions.tip: Nublado has nube (cloud) inside - a nubby, cloudy sky!

questions.q: How do you ask What is the weather like? in Spanish?
questions.explain: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather. ¿Qué hora es? asks the time.
questions.tip: Tiempo means both time and weather - the weather changes over time!

questions.explain: Camisa means shirt.
questions.tip: Camisa: come see my new shirt!

questions.explain: Pantalones means pants.
questions.tip: Pantalones has 'pant' right inside it!

questions.explain: Zapatos means shoes.
questions.tip: Zapatos: zap! You zip into your shoes and run!

questions.explain: Sombrero means hat (any hat, not only the wide one).
questions.tip: Sombrero comes from sombra (shade) - a hat shades your face!

questions.explain: Vestido means dress. A vest is un chaleco.
questions.tip: Vestido comes from vestir (to dress) - a dress!

questions.explain: Falda means skirt.
questions.tip: Falda sounds like 'fold-a' - fold your skirt neatly!

questions.explain: Calcetines means socks. In some countries people also say medias.
questions.tip: Calcetines: socks for your teeny toes!

questions.explain: Chaqueta means jacket.
questions.tip: Chaqueta sounds like 'jacket-a'!

questions.explain: La cocina is the kitchen. Cocinar means to cook.
questions.tip: Cocina sounds like 'cuisine' - cooking happens in the kitchen!

questions.explain: El baño is the bathroom.
questions.tip: Baño: BAH-nyo, time for a bath!

questions.explain: El dormitorio is the bedroom. People also say el cuarto, and in Mexico la recámara.
questions.tip: Dormitorio is like 'dormitory' - a place to sleep!

questions.explain: La cama is the bed.
questions.tip: Cama: come-a to bed!

questions.explain: La puerta is the door.
questions.tip: Puerta sounds like 'portal' - a door is a portal!

questions.explain: La ventana is the window.
questions.tip: Ventana sounds like 'vent' - a window lets air in!

questions.explain: La sala is the living room.
questions.tip: Sala sounds like 'salon' - a room where people sit together!

questions.q: How do you say house in Spanish?
questions.explain: Casa means house. Cosa means thing and caja means box.
questions.tip: Mi casa es su casa - my house is your house!

questions.explain: With yo (I), ser becomes soy: Yo soy estudiante.
questions.tip: Soy rhymes with boy - I am a boy, I am a girl: soy!

questions.explain: With tú (you), ser becomes eres.
questions.tip: Tú eres - you are, both with an r sound!

questions.explain: Ella tiene diez años. In Spanish you have years: tener años means to be a certain age.
questions.tip: Picture holding a birthday cake with ten candles - you HAVE ten years!

questions.explain: With ellos (they), tener becomes tienen.
questions.tip: Add an -n for they: tiene becomes tienen!

questions.explain: With nosotros (we), ir becomes vamos.
questions.tip: ¡Vamos! is a cheer: Let's go!

questions.explain: With yo, ir becomes voy: Yo voy al parque.
questions.tip: Voy rhymes with boy - the boy says I go!

questions.q: What does the verb ir mean?
questions.explain: Ir means to go. Tener is to have and ser is to be.
questions.tip: Ir is short and fast - go, go, go!

questions.explain: Tengo hambre means I am hungry (literally, I have hunger).
questions.tip: Hambre sounds like 'hamburger' - I'm hungry for a hamburger!

questions.q: What does Tengo ocho años mean?
questions.explain: Tener + años tells your age: Tengo ocho años means I am 8 years old.
questions.tip: In Spanish you HAVE your years, like candles on a cake!

g35.name: Gender of Nouns: el and la

questions.q: Which word goes before perro? ___ perro
questions.explain: Perro is masculine, so it is el perro.
questions.tip: Perro ends in -o, so it gets el!

questions.q: Which word goes before casa? ___ casa
questions.explain: Casa is feminine, so it is la casa.
questions.tip: Casa ends in -a: la-la-la, la casa!

questions.q: Which word goes before mano? ___ mano
questions.explain: Mano ends in -o but is feminine: la mano. It is a special case.
questions.tip: La mano is a rule-breaker - a hand waving la la la!

questions.q: Which word goes before día? ___ día
questions.explain: Día ends in -a but is masculine: el día.
questions.tip: Buenos días: buenos is masculine, so it's el día!

questions.q: Which word goes before mapa? ___ mapa
questions.explain: Mapa is masculine even though it ends in -a: el mapa.
questions.tip: Some words ending in -a are rule-breakers that take el: el mapa, el problema, el planeta!

questions.q: Which word goes before flor? ___ flor
questions.explain: Flor is feminine: la flor.
questions.tip: La flor: a pretty flower in la-la land!

questions.q: Which word goes before libro? ___ libro
questions.explain: Libro is masculine: el libro.
questions.tip: El goes with -o: el libro!

questions.q: Most Spanish nouns that end in -o are...
questions.explain: Most nouns ending in -o are masculine and most ending in -a are feminine, with some exceptions.
questions.tip: O for el, A for la - most of the time!

questions.q: Which word goes before mesa? ___ mesa
questions.explain: Mesa is feminine: la mesa.
questions.tip: Mesa ends in -a: la mesa!

questions.q: What is the plural of libro?
questions.explain: Words ending in a vowel add -s: libros.
questions.tip: Ends in a vowel? Just add -s!

questions.q: What is the plural of flor?
questions.explain: Words ending in a consonant add -es: flores.
questions.tip: Ends in a consonant? Add -es!

questions.q: What is the plural of lápiz?
questions.explain: A final z changes to c before -es: lápices.
questions.tip: Z and E don't hold hands - z turns into c: lápices!

questions.q: What is the plural of el gato?
questions.explain: El becomes los in the plural: los gatos.
questions.tip: El grows up into los in the plural!

questions.q: What is the plural of la casa?
questions.explain: La becomes las in the plural: las casas.
questions.tip: La grows up into las in the plural!

questions.q: What is the plural of árbol?
questions.explain: Árbol ends in a consonant, so add -es: árboles.
questions.tip: Árbol ends in L, a consonant, so add -es!

questions.q: What is the plural of pez?
questions.explain: The z changes to c: un pez, dos peces.
questions.tip: Pez to peces: z can't stand next to e!

questions.q: What is the plural of mujer?
questions.explain: Mujer ends in r, so add -es: mujeres.
questions.tip: Mujer ends in R: add -es, mujeres!

questions.explain: For -ar verbs, yo takes -o: hablo.
questions.tip: Yo always ends in -o: hablo, I talk!

questions.explain: For -er verbs, tú takes -es: comes.
questions.tip: Tú loves the letter S: comes, hablas, vives!

questions.explain: -ir verbs use -imos for nosotros: vivimos. -er verbs use -emos.
questions.tip: -IR verbs keep their i for nosotros: vivir becomes vivimos!

questions.explain: Ellos takes -en for -ir verbs: escriben.
questions.tip: They need an N: ellos escriben!

questions.q: estudiar, ella: Ella ___ todos los días.
questions.explain: Él, ella and usted take -a for -ar verbs: estudia.
questions.tip: -AR verbs keep their A: estudiar becomes estudia!

questions.explain: -er verbs use -emos for nosotros in the present: aprendemos.
questions.tip: -ER verbs keep their E: aprender becomes aprendemos!

questions.explain: Ustedes takes -an for -ar verbs: bailan.
questions.tip: Ustedes and ellos share the -n ending: bailan!

questions.explain: Yo takes -o: bebo.
questions.tip: Yo always ends in -o: bebo!

questions.explain: -ir verbs use -es for tú: abres.
questions.tip: -ER and -IR verbs are twins except for nosotros and vosotros!

questions.q: What ending do -ar verbs use for nosotros in the present tense?
questions.explain: Hablar becomes hablamos, cantar becomes cantamos.
questions.tip: Nosotros keeps the verb's own vowel: -ar gives -amos!

questions.explain: Use ser for professions: Mi madre es doctora.
questions.tip: SER is for DOCTOR: Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship!

questions.explain: Use estar for temporary states and feelings: estoy cansado.
questions.tip: For how you feel and where you are, use the verb estar!

questions.explain: For where an event takes place, use ser: La fiesta es en mi casa.
questions.tip: Events take place with SER: where the party is happening!

questions.explain: Use estar for the location of places and things: Madrid está en España.
questions.tip: ESTAR is for PLACE: Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion!

questions.explain: Use ser for days and dates: Hoy es lunes.
questions.tip: Days are the T (Time) in DOCTOR, so use SER!

questions.explain: Use ser for origin: Somos de México.
questions.tip: Origin is the O in DOCTOR: somos de!

questions.explain: Use estar for a condition at the moment: La sopa está fría.
questions.tip: Soup cools down - a changing condition, so ESTAR!

questions.explain: ¿Cómo estás? asks how you are feeling. ¿Cómo eres? asks what you are like.
questions.tip: How you feel is how you are: ¿Cómo estás?

questions.explain: Use estar for where people are: Están en la biblioteca.
questions.tip: Where you are, near or far? Always estar!

questions.q: Which verb do you use to say where a person or thing is located?
questions.explain: Estar is used for location: El libro está en la mesa.
questions.tip: For how you feel and where you are, always use the verb estar!

questions.explain: Casa is feminine singular, so the adjective is blanca.
questions.tip: Adjectives copy the noun's outfit: la casa wears -a, so blanca!

questions.explain: Perros is masculine plural: pequeños.
questions.tip: Many boy dogs: -o for masculine, plus -s for more!

questions.explain: Chicas is feminine plural: altas.
questions.tip: Many girls: -as, like las chicas altas!

questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -e do not change for gender: la clase interesante, el libro interesante.
questions.tip: -E adjectives are flexible friends - they fit any gender!

questions.q: In Spanish, where do most descriptive adjectives go?
questions.explain: Most go after the noun: un carro rojo (a red car).
questions.tip: Noun first, then the description: el carro rojo!

questions.explain: Flores is feminine plural: rojas.
questions.tip: Flores are feminine and many: rojas!

questions.explain: Ella is feminine singular: simpática.
questions.tip: Ella ends in -a, so simpática ends in -a!

questions.explain: Azul ends in a consonant, so the plural adds -es: azules. It does not change for gender.
questions.tip: Azul ends in L, so add -es, like árboles!

questions.explain: Verde does not change for gender; just add -s for plural: verdes.
questions.tip: Verde is a flexible -e friend: just add -s!

questions.explain: ¿Dónde? means where? ¿Dónde está el baño?
questions.tip: Dónde sounds like 'don-day' - where did Don go today?

questions.explain: ¿Cuándo? means when?
questions.tip: Cuándo sounds like 'KWAN-do' - when is karate class?

questions.explain: ¿Quién? means who? The plural is ¿Quiénes?
questions.tip: Quién sounds like 'key-en' - who has the key?

questions.explain: ¿Por qué? means why? The answer often starts with porque (because).
questions.tip: Por qué literally asks 'for what?' - that's why!

questions.explain: Porque (one word, no accent) means because.
questions.tip: Porque is one word because it answers in one go!

questions.explain: Años is masculine plural, so use ¿Cuántos? ¿Cuántos años tienes? means How old are you?
questions.tip: Cuánto sounds like 'quantity' - how many!

questions.explain: ¿Qué? means what? ¿Qué es esto? means What is this?
questions.tip: Qué sounds like 'kay' - okay, what is it?

questions.explain: ¿Cómo? means how? ¿Cómo estás? means How are you?
questions.tip: Cómo sounds like 'how come' - how?

questions.explain: ¿Cuánto? means how much: ¿Cuánto cuesta? asks the price.
questions.tip: Cuánto = quantity and cuesta = cost: how much does it cost?

questions.q: Spanish question words like qué and dónde carry a written accent when they ask a question.
questions.explain: True. Question words have an accent: ¿qué?, ¿dónde?, ¿cuándo?
questions.tip: Question words wear a hat (accent) when they ask!

questions.q: What time is it? Es la una.
questions.explain: Es la una means It is one o'clock.
questions.tip: One o'clock is lonely and singular: es la una!

questions.q: What time is it? Son las tres.
questions.explain: Son las tres means It is three o'clock.
questions.tip: Son las + a number for every hour except one!

questions.q: What time is it? Son las dos y media.
questions.explain: Y media means half past: 2:30.
questions.tip: Media means half, like a medium is in the middle!

questions.q: What time is it? Son las cuatro y cuarto.
questions.explain: Y cuarto means a quarter past: 4:15.
questions.tip: Cuarto means quarter: a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes!

questions.q: What time is it? Son las ocho menos diez.
questions.explain: Menos diez means ten minutes before: ten to eight is 7:50.
questions.tip: Menos means minus: eight minus ten minutes is 7:50!

questions.q: How do you ask What time is it?
questions.explain: ¿Qué hora es? asks the time.
questions.tip: Hora sounds like 'hour' - what hour is it?

questions.q: Why do we say Es la una but Son las dos?
choices: Una is singular; other hours are plural
questions.explain: One o'clock is one hour (singular, es); other hours are plural (son).
questions.tip: One hour, one es; more hours, son!

questions.q: How do you say at three o'clock?
questions.explain: Use a las to say at what time: La clase es a las tres.
questions.tip: A las means at the - at the third hour!

questions.q: What time is it? Son las nueve de la noche.
questions.explain: De la noche means at night, so it is 9 PM. De la mañana means AM.
questions.tip: Noche sounds like nachos - a nighttime, PM snack!

questions.explain: Lo siento means I'm sorry.
questions.tip: Lo siento literally means I feel it - I feel sorry!

questions.explain: No entiendo means I don't understand. No sé means I don't know.
questions.tip: Entiendo sounds like 'intend' - I don't get what you intend!

questions.q: How do you ask How do you say ... in Spanish?
questions.explain: ¿Cómo se dice ... en español? asks how to say something.
questions.tip: Dice comes from decir, to say: how is it said?

questions.explain: ¿Qué significa? means What does it mean?
questions.tip: Significa sounds like 'signify' - what does it signify?

questions.q: What does Tengo que estudiar mean?
questions.explain: Tener que + infinitive means to have to do something.
questions.tip: Tener que: have + que = have to!

questions.q: What does Me gusta el fútbol mean?
questions.explain: Me gusta means I like (literally, it pleases me).
questions.tip: Gusto means enjoyment: me gusta, I enjoy it!

questions.explain: ¡Buena suerte! means Good luck!
questions.tip: Suerte rhymes with fuerte (strong) - be strong and lucky!

questions.q: What does ¿Puedo ir al baño? mean?
choices: May I go to the bathroom?
questions.explain: ¿Puedo...? means May I...? or Can I...?
questions.tip: Puedo is from poder, like 'power' - do I have the power to go?

questions.q: You need to squeeze past someone. What do you say?
questions.explain: Con permiso means excuse me when you need to pass by. Buen provecho means enjoy your meal.
questions.tip: Permiso sounds like 'permission' - may I pass?

questions.explain: Ayer marks a completed action at a specific time, so use the preterite: comí.
questions.tip: Ayer (yesterday) means a done deal: preterite!

questions.q: Cuando era niño, ___ en el parque todos los días. (jugar, yo)
questions.explain: Habitual past actions (todos los días) use the imperfect: jugaba.
questions.tip: Used to and every day mean imperfect: -aba, -ía!

questions.explain: A single completed action last night uses the preterite: habló. (Hablo without the accent means I speak.)
questions.tip: Anoche, last night, one finished action: preterite!

questions.q: Which tense describes background in the past, like weather, time or age?
questions.explain: The imperfect sets the scene: Hacía frío. Eran las ocho. Tenía diez años.
questions.tip: The imperfect paints the background; the preterite is the action on stage!

questions.q: Eran las ocho cuando ___ mi padre. (llegar)
questions.explain: The arrival is a completed event that interrupts the background, so use the preterite: llegó.
questions.tip: Background (eran) + interruption (llegó) = imperfect + preterite!

questions.explain: An action in progress that gets interrupted uses the imperfect: leía.
questions.tip: Mientras (while) signals the long action that gets interrupted: imperfect!

questions.q: What is the preterite of ir for yo?
questions.explain: Fui. Ir and ser share the same preterite forms; context tells them apart.
questions.tip: Fui does double duty: I went and I was!

questions.q: What is the preterite of tener for yo?
questions.explain: Tener has an irregular stem in the preterite: tuve, tuviste, tuvo...
questions.tip: Tener grows a U in the preterite: tuve, tuviste, tuvo!

questions.q: What is the imperfect of ser for nosotros?
questions.explain: Ser is irregular in the imperfect: era, eras, era, éramos, eran.
questions.tip: Éramos: we were a team!

questions.q: What is the preterite of hacer for él?
questions.explain: Hacer: hice, hiciste, hizo. The c changes to z before o.
questions.tip: Hizo uses a z so it doesn't sound like 'ico'!

questions.explain: The future adds -é to the infinitive for yo: hablaré.
questions.tip: The future is easy: keep the whole infinitive and add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án!

questions.q: What is the future of tener for yo?
questions.explain: Tener has the irregular future stem tendr-: tendré.
questions.tip: Tener, poner, salir and venir add a D: tendré, pondré, saldré, vendré!

questions.q: What is the future of hacer for ella?
questions.explain: Hacer uses the stem har-: hará.
questions.tip: Hacer and decir shrink in the future: haré, diré!

questions.q: What is the future of decir for nosotros?
questions.explain: Decir uses the stem dir-: diremos.
questions.tip: Decir shrinks to dir- for the future!

questions.q: What is the future of poder for tú?
questions.explain: Poder drops the e: podr-, so podrás.
questions.tip: Poder, saber and haber drop the e: podré, sabré, habré!

questions.q: What is the future of salir for ellos?
questions.explain: Salir uses the stem saldr-: saldrán.
questions.tip: Salir adds a D, just like tener: saldrán!

questions.q: What is the future of ir for nosotros?
questions.explain: Ir is regular in the future: iré, irás, irá, iremos, irán.
questions.tip: Ir + -emos = iremos - no tricks!

questions.q: What does Voy a estudiar mean?
questions.explain: Ir a + infinitive is a very common way to talk about the near future.
questions.tip: Ir a + infinitive is like 'gonna' in English!

questions.q: What does ¿Dónde estará Juan? usually mean?
questions.explain: The future tense can express a guess about the present: I wonder where Juan is.
questions.tip: The future can wonder: estará means he's probably!

questions.explain: The reflexive pronoun for yo is me: me levanto (I get up).
questions.tip: Reflexive pronouns are a mirror: yo looks in the mirror and sees me!

questions.q: What does Ella se ducha mean?
questions.explain: Ducharse means to take a shower.
questions.tip: Ducks love water, and ducharse means taking a shower!

questions.explain: The reflexive pronoun for nosotros is nos: nos acostamos (we go to bed).
questions.tip: Nosotros looks in the mirror and sees nos!

questions.explain: Ellos uses se: se lavan las manos (they wash their hands).
questions.tip: Se is the busy one: him, her, them and usted!

questions.explain: Tú uses te: te despiertas (you wake up).
questions.tip: Tú and te are a matching pair!

questions.q: Which verb means to get dressed?
questions.explain: Vestirse is to get dressed. Ponerse is to put on (an item) and quitarse is to take off.
questions.tip: Vestirse: get dressed, maybe in a vest!

questions.q: What does Me cepillo los dientes mean?
questions.explain: With reflexive verbs Spanish uses los, not mis, for body parts: Me cepillo los dientes.
questions.tip: Spanish already knows the teeth are yours - so los, not mis!

questions.explain: The pronoun attaches to the infinitive and matches the subject: Voy a bañarme (or Me voy a bañar).
questions.tip: The mirror pronoun follows the person: yo goes with me, so bañarme!

questions.explain: Llamarse is reflexive: literally How do you call yourself? It means What is your name?
questions.tip: Llamarse: you call yourself by your name!

questions.explain: El libro is masculine singular, so the direct object pronoun is lo.
questions.tip: Lo for a masculine thing, la for a feminine one - just like el and la!

questions.explain: Las manzanas is feminine plural: las compré.
questions.tip: Las manzanas, las compré - the pronoun matches the article!

questions.explain: María is the direct object (feminine): la veo.
questions.tip: María is a she, so la!

questions.q: ___ doy un regalo a mi madre.
questions.explain: A mi madre is the indirect object (to whom), so use le.
questions.tip: Le answers to whom: to him, to her!

questions.q: Le doy el libro a Ana. Replace both objects: ___ doy.
questions.explain: Le changes to se before lo or la: Se lo doy.
questions.tip: Le lo sounds like lelo (silly), so it changes to se lo!

questions.explain: The indirect object pronoun for us is nos.
questions.tip: Nos is us, like nosotros!

questions.q: Which is another correct way to say Voy a comprarlo?
questions.explain: With an infinitive, the pronoun can attach to it or go before the conjugated verb.
questions.tip: Pronouns can hop in front of the verb or ride on the infinitive's back!

questions.explain: Me is the object (me), and ayudas is you help: Will you help me?
questions.tip: Me means me: ¿Me ayudas? Help me!

questions.q: Give it (el libro) to me! (tú command)
questions.explain: In affirmative commands, pronouns attach to the end, indirect before direct: Dámelo. An accent keeps the stress.
questions.tip: Commands are magnets: pronouns stick to the end - Dámelo!

questions.explain: Para marks the recipient: This gift is for you.
questions.tip: Para is for the person who gets the present!

questions.explain: Por means through or around: We walk through the park.
questions.tip: Por means passing through, like walking through a door!

questions.explain: Gracias por: thanks for (because of) your help.
questions.tip: Gracias por: thanks because of - por is for the cause!

questions.explain: Para + infinitive expresses purpose: in order to be a doctor.
questions.tip: Para points to a goal: in order to!

questions.explain: Por is used for exchange: I paid ten dollars for the shirt.
questions.tip: Por is for swaps: money for a shirt!

questions.explain: Para marks a destination: We leave for Madrid tomorrow.
questions.tip: Para points like an arrow to where you're going!

questions.explain: Para marks a deadline: The homework is due Monday.
questions.tip: Para for a deadline: due by Monday!

questions.explain: Por marks the means of communication: by phone.
questions.tip: Por the phone - by means of!

questions.explain: Por la mañana means in the morning (during that part of the day).
questions.tip: Por la mañana: during the morning!

questions.explain: The verb agrees with what is liked. Los perros is plural, so gustan.
questions.tip: With gustar, the thing liked is the boss of the verb: plural things, gustan!

questions.explain: With an infinitive (bailar), use the singular gusta.
questions.tip: Activities count as one: me gusta bailar!

questions.explain: A nosotros pairs with nos: Nos encanta la música.
questions.tip: A nosotros needs nos - they come as a pair!

questions.explain: For they, the indirect object pronoun is les.
questions.tip: Les is for them, with an -s like ellos!

questions.q: What does Me duele la cabeza mean?
questions.explain: Doler works like gustar: the head hurts me.
questions.tip: Doler sounds like 'dolor' - pain!

questions.explain: Los ojos is plural, so duelen: My eyes hurt.
questions.tip: Two eyes, two hurts: duelen!

questions.q: What does Me interesa la historia mean?
questions.explain: Interesar works like gustar: history interests me.
questions.tip: Interesar works backwards: history interests me!

questions.q: What does Me molesta el ruido mean?
questions.explain: Molestar means to bother, not to molest.
questions.tip: Molestar is like a mosquito buzzing in your ear - it bothers you!

questions.q: What does Me falta un lápiz mean?
questions.explain: Faltar works like gustar: a pencil is lacking to me.
questions.tip: Faltar sounds like 'fault' - it's not my fault I'm missing a pencil!

questions.explain: El aeropuerto is the airport. The airplane is el avión.
questions.tip: Aero + puerto (port): an air port!

questions.explain: La maleta is the suitcase.
questions.tip: Maleta sounds like 'mallet' - don't pack a mallet in your suitcase!

questions.explain: El boleto is a ticket in Latin America. In Spain people say el billete.
questions.tip: Boleto sounds like 'ballot' - but it's a ticket, not a vote!

questions.explain: La tarea is homework.
questions.tip: Tarea starts like 'task' - your homework task!

questions.explain: El horario is the schedule or timetable.
questions.tip: Horario has hora (hour) inside - a list of hours!

questions.explain: La fiebre is fever.
questions.tip: Fiebre sounds like 'fever'!

questions.explain: La farmacia is the pharmacy. A farm is una granja.
questions.tip: Farmacia sounds like 'pharmacy' - ph and f make the same sound!

questions.q: What does Me siento mal mean?
questions.explain: Sentirse mal means to feel bad or sick.
questions.tip: Sentirse is like 'sense': I sense I'm sick!

questions.explain: La salida is the exit. The entrance is la entrada.
questions.tip: Salir means to leave, so la salida is how you leave!

questions.q: At the doctor, what is la receta?
questions.explain: La receta is a prescription (and also a recipe). A receipt is un recibo.
questions.tip: A prescription is the doctor's receta (recipe) for getting well!

questions.explain: Wanting someone else to do something triggers the subjunctive: vengas.
questions.tip: WEIRDO triggers the subjunctive: Wishes, Emotions, Impersonal expressions, Recommendations, Doubt, Ojalá!

questions.explain: Hope (esperar que) takes the subjunctive: estén.
questions.tip: Hope is an Emotion in WEIRDO - subjunctive!

questions.explain: Impersonal expressions of importance take the subjunctive: estudiemos.
questions.tip: Impersonal expressions are the I in WEIRDO!

questions.explain: Doubt triggers the subjunctive. Saber is irregular: sepa.
questions.tip: Doubt is the D in WEIRDO: dudo que + subjunctive!

questions.explain: Creer que in the affirmative expresses belief, so it takes the indicative: tiene.
questions.tip: Belief is certainty: creo que takes the indicative, no creo que flips to subjunctive!

questions.explain: No creer que expresses doubt and takes the subjunctive: sea.
questions.tip: No creo = doubt, and doubt is the D in WEIRDO!

questions.q: Cuando ___ a casa, te llamo. (llegar, yo)
questions.explain: Cuando referring to a future event takes the subjunctive: llegue (g becomes gu before e).
questions.tip: Cuando + a future event = not real yet = subjunctive!

questions.explain: The apartment is hypothetical (not yet known to exist), so use the subjunctive: tenga.
questions.tip: If it might not exist, it's subjunctive: a dream apartment!

questions.explain: Ojalá expresses a wish and takes the subjunctive: llueva.
questions.tip: Ojalá is the O in WEIRDO - always subjunctive!

questions.q: What is the present subjunctive of ir for yo?
questions.explain: Ir is irregular in the subjunctive: vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayan.
questions.tip: DISHES: dar, ir, saber, haber, estar, ser are the irregular subjunctive verbs!

questions.explain: A past-tense trigger (quería) takes the past subjunctive: vinieras.
questions.tip: Past trigger, past subjunctive: quería que leads to vinieras!

questions.explain: Contrary-to-fact si clauses use past subjunctive + conditional: Si tuviera..., viajaría.
questions.tip: Si + -ra, then -ría: si tuviera, viajaría!

questions.q: Me pidió que ___ más despacio. (hablar, yo)
questions.explain: A past request (pidió) takes the past subjunctive: hablara.
questions.tip: Pidió is past, so hablara follows!

questions.explain: The nosotros form of the past subjunctive carries an accent: saliéramos.
questions.tip: Nosotros always gets an accent in the past subjunctive: -áramos, -iéramos!

questions.q: The past subjunctive is formed from which form?
questions.explain: Take ellos preterite (hablaron, tuvieron), drop -ron, add -ra endings: hablara, tuviera.
questions.tip: Ellos preterite, chop off -ron, add -ra: tuvieron becomes tuviera!

questions.q: Si yo ___ tú, no lo haría. (ser)
questions.explain: If I were you: Si yo fuera tú.
questions.tip: If I were you: Si yo fuera tú - fuera is the famous one!

questions.explain: Como si (as if) always takes the past subjunctive: supiera.
questions.tip: Como si is always as if it were unreal - past subjunctive!

questions.q: Hablase is a correct alternative form of hablara.
questions.explain: True. The -se forms are equivalent; they are more common in Spain and in formal writing.
questions.tip: -ra or -se, both are okay!

questions.explain: Ojalá + past subjunctive expresses an unlikely or contrary-to-fact wish: I wish I could help you.
questions.tip: Ojalá + past subjunctive is a wishful sigh: if only!

questions.explain: The conditional adds -ía to the infinitive: comería (I would eat).
questions.tip: Would = -ía: comería, I would eat!

questions.q: What is the conditional of tener for ella?
questions.explain: The conditional uses the same irregular stems as the future: tendr-, so tendría.
questions.tip: The conditional borrows the future's irregular stems: tendr- + -ía!

questions.explain: The conditional softens requests: ¿Podría usted ayudarme? (Could you help me?)
questions.tip: Could you? = ¿Podría? - the polite power word!

questions.q: What is the conditional of hacer for nosotros?
questions.explain: Hacer uses the stem har-: haríamos.
questions.tip: Har- from the future + -íamos!

questions.explain: Me gustaría is the conditional of gustar: I would like.
questions.tip: Gustaría is would like - the polite way to order!

questions.q: What is the conditional of decir for ellos?
questions.explain: Decir uses the stem dir-: dirían.
questions.tip: Dir- stem from the future, plus -ían!

questions.q: Si tuviera tiempo, ___ al cine. (ir, yo)
questions.explain: The result clause of a contrary-to-fact condition uses the conditional: iría.
questions.tip: Si tuviera... iría: -ra then -ría!

questions.q: What does Serían las diez cuando llegó usually mean?
choices: It will be ten when he arrives.
It was probably about ten when he arrived.
It would be ten if he arrived.
questions.explain: The conditional can express a guess about the past: It was probably ten o'clock.
questions.tip: Future guesses about now; conditional guesses about then!

questions.explain: The present perfect uses haber: he comido (I have eaten).
questions.tip: He, has, ha, hemos, han - haber is the helper!

questions.q: What is the past participle of escribir?
questions.explain: Escribir has an irregular participle: escrito.
questions.tip: Escrito is like 'script' - something written!

questions.explain: Ver has an irregular participle: visto. The participle does not change after haber.
questions.tip: Visto sounds like 'vista' - a view you have seen!

questions.q: What is the past participle of hacer?
questions.explain: Hacer becomes hecho: He hecho la tarea.
questions.tip: Dicho y hecho - said and done!

questions.q: Para mañana, yo ___ terminado el proyecto.
questions.explain: The future perfect (habré terminado) says something will be done by a future time.
questions.tip: Habré = will have: the future of haber!

questions.explain: Abrir has an irregular participle: abierto. After haber it stays masculine singular.
questions.tip: Abierto: a bear opened the door!

questions.explain: The conditional perfect (habría + participle) means would have.
questions.tip: Habría = would have!

questions.explain: Present perfect subjunctive: hayas dormido (I hope you have slept well).
questions.tip: Hayas is haber in the subjunctive after espero que!

questions.q: What is the past participle of volver?
questions.explain: Volver becomes vuelto: Ha vuelto (He has returned).
questions.tip: Volver gives vuelto: the boomerang has returned!

questions.q: What is the past participle of romper?
questions.explain: Romper becomes roto: Se ha roto el vaso.
questions.tip: Roto rhymes with 'photo' - a broken photo frame!

questions.q: What does estar en las nubes mean?
questions.explain: Literally to be in the clouds: to be distracted or daydreaming.
questions.tip: Head in the clouds = en las nubes!

questions.q: What does tomarle el pelo a alguien mean?
questions.explain: Literally to take someone's hair: to tease or fool someone.
questions.tip: Spanish pulls your hair instead of your leg!

questions.q: What does costar un ojo de la cara mean?
choices: To cost an arm and a leg
questions.explain: Literally to cost an eye from the face: to be very expensive.
questions.tip: An eye instead of an arm and a leg - both are expensive!

questions.q: What does ser pan comido mean?
choices: To be a piece of cake
questions.explain: Literally to be eaten bread: something very easy.
questions.tip: Eaten bread and a piece of cake - easy food, easy task!

questions.q: What does meter la pata mean?
choices: To put your foot in it
questions.explain: Literally to put in the paw: to make a blunder.
questions.tip: Foot in your mouth, paw in the mess!

questions.q: What does echar de menos mean?
questions.explain: Echar de menos means to miss. In Latin America extrañar is also very common.
questions.tip: Echar de menos: you feel less when someone is missing!

questions.q: What does estar como pez en el agua mean?
questions.explain: Literally like a fish in water: completely comfortable.
questions.tip: A fish in water is in its element!

questions.q: What does dar en el clavo mean?
choices: To hit the nail on the head
questions.explain: Literally to hit the nail: to get something exactly right.
questions.tip: Clavo means nail - both languages hit the nail!

questions.q: What does no tener pelos en la lengua mean?
questions.explain: Literally to have no hairs on the tongue: to say what you think directly.
questions.tip: No hairs on the tongue means nothing slows your words down!

questions.q: What does llover a cántaros mean?
questions.explain: Literally to rain by the pitcher: to pour.
questions.tip: Cántaros are pitchers - rain pouring like from a jug!

questions.q: What does actual mean in Spanish?
questions.explain: Actual means current or present-day. Actually is en realidad.
questions.tip: Actual = actualmente = currently: a current event!

questions.explain: A librería sells books. A library is una biblioteca.
questions.tip: Libro + -ería makes a shop, like panadería (bakery) - you buy books there!

questions.explain: Realizar means to carry out. To realize something is darse cuenta.
questions.tip: Realizar makes something real - it carries it out!

questions.q: What does sensible mean in Spanish?
questions.explain: Sensible means sensitive. Sensible in English is sensato.
questions.tip: Spanish sensible feels a lot: it's sensitive!

questions.q: What does asistir a clase mean?
questions.explain: Asistir a means to attend. To help is ayudar.
questions.tip: Asistir a = attend; to assist = ayudar!

questions.explain: Carpeta means folder. A carpet is una alfombra.
questions.tip: A carpeta holds papers; an alfombra covers floors!

questions.explain: Recordar means to remember or remind. To record is grabar.
questions.tip: Recordar comes from Latin cor (heart): bring back to the heart!

questions.explain: Molestar simply means to bother or annoy.
questions.tip: Molestar = annoy, like a mosquito!

questions.explain: Introducir means to insert or bring in. To introduce a person is presentar.
questions.tip: Introducir una tarjeta: insert a card!

questions.explain: Lectura means a reading. A lecture is una conferencia or una clase.
questions.tip: Lectura comes from leer (to read)!

questions.q: What does ¿Dónde está el baño? mean?
questions.explain: ¿Dónde está...? asks where something is.
questions.tip: ¿Dónde está? - estar for location, always!

questions.explain: ¿Cuánto cuesta? asks the price.
questions.tip: Cuesta sounds like 'cost-a'!

questions.q: What does Quisiera una habitación para dos noches mean?
choices: I would like a room for two nights.
questions.explain: Quisiera is a polite I would like; una habitación is a hotel room.
questions.tip: Habitación sounds like 'habitat' - your room is your habitat!

questions.q: What does ¿A qué hora sale el tren? mean?
choices: What time does the train leave?
questions.explain: Salir means to leave; llegar means to arrive.
questions.tip: Salir = to leave, and salida = exit!

questions.q: How do you ask for a round-trip ticket?
choices: un boleto de ida y vuelta
questions.explain: De ida y vuelta is round trip; de ida is one way. In Spain, billete instead of boleto.
questions.tip: Ida (going) y vuelta (return): there and back!

questions.q: What does Doble a la derecha mean?
questions.explain: A la derecha is to the right; a la izquierda is to the left.
questions.tip: Derecha = right; izquierda = left - I zig left!

questions.explain: Derecho here means straight ahead. In Spain people often say todo recto.
questions.tip: Derecho sounds like 'direct' - straight ahead!

questions.explain: Me is the object: Can you (usted) help me?
questions.tip: Me puede: me first, then the verb - can you help me?

questions.q: How do you say I am lost (said by a man)?
questions.explain: Being lost is a state, so use estar: Estoy perdido (a woman says perdida).
questions.tip: Perdido comes from perder, to lose - you've lost your way!

questions.q: What is la parada de autobús?
questions.explain: La parada is the stop. Bus also varies by country: camión (Mexico), guagua (Caribbean).
questions.tip: Parada sounds like 'parade' - the bus stops for the parade!

questions.q: What does La cuenta, por favor mean?
questions.explain: La cuenta is the bill or check.
questions.tip: Cuenta comes from contar, to count - they count up your bill!

questions.explain: Recomendar is to recommend; this uses the usted form for the server.
questions.tip: Recomienda sounds like 'recommend'!

questions.q: How do you say I'm allergic to shellfish (said by a man)?
questions.explain: Soy alérgico a... (a woman says alérgica). Los mariscos are shellfish and seafood.
questions.tip: Mariscos come from the mar (sea)!

questions.q: What does Para mí, el pollo mean when ordering?
questions.explain: Para mí... is a common way to order: For me, the chicken.
questions.tip: Para mí - for me!

questions.explain: La propina is the tip.
questions.tip: Propina: give the waiter a pro tip!

questions.q: What does Una mesa para cuatro, por favor mean?
questions.explain: Mesa means table.
questions.tip: Mesa is a table, like a flat-topped mesa mountain!

questions.q: In Mexico, what is el mesero?
questions.explain: Mesero is used in Mexico and Central America; camarero in Spain; mozo in Argentina.
questions.tip: The mesero serves the mesa!

questions.q: What does ¿Está incluido el servicio? mean?
questions.explain: El servicio here refers to the service charge or tip.
questions.tip: Servicio = service = the tip!

questions.q: What does ¿Me trae agua, por favor? mean?
choices: Could you bring me water, please?
questions.explain: Traer means to bring: Could you bring me water?
questions.tip: Traer = to bring, like a tray carrying water!

questions.explain: Buen provecho is said to people who are eating. Cheers is ¡Salud!
questions.tip: Provecho sounds like 'profit' - may you profit from your food!

questions.q: How do you shout Help! in Spanish?
questions.explain: ¡Socorro! or ¡Ayuda! both mean Help!
questions.tip: Socorro sounds like 'succor', an old English word for help!

questions.q: What does Llame a una ambulancia mean?
questions.explain: Llame is the usted command of llamar (to call).
questions.tip: Llame comes from llamar, to call!

questions.q: What does Necesito un médico mean?
questions.explain: Médico means doctor; medicine is medicina or medicamento.
questions.tip: Médico sounds like 'medic'!

questions.q: What does ¿Dónde está el hospital más cercano? mean?
questions.explain: Más cercano means nearest.
questions.tip: Cercano is near, as in close by!

questions.q: What does Me robaron la cartera mean?
questions.explain: Robar is to steal; la cartera is the wallet (in some countries, a purse).
questions.tip: Robar sounds like 'rob'!

questions.explain: Un incendio is a fire that is burning out of control, like a house fire.
questions.tip: Incendio sounds like 'incendiary' - fire!

questions.q: What does Me duele el pecho mean?
questions.explain: El pecho is the chest. Back is la espalda; stomach is el estómago.
questions.tip: Pecho rhymes with techo (roof) - your chest is the roof over your heart!

questions.q: What does Perdí mi pasaporte mean?
questions.explain: Perdí is the preterite of perder (to lose).
questions.tip: Perder = to lose: perdí, I lost!

questions.explain: ¡Cuidado! is a warning: Watch out! or Be careful!
questions.tip: ¡Cuidado! is like 'take care' shouted fast!

questions.q: How do you say I need help?
questions.explain: Necesitar + noun: Necesito ayuda.
questions.tip: Ayuda sounds like 'aid' - I need aid!

questions.q: Which form of you do you use with an older stranger?
questions.explain: Usted is the respectful form for strangers, elders and formal situations.
questions.tip: Usted for elders and strangers - show respect!

questions.explain: Usted takes third-person verb forms: ¿Cómo está usted?
questions.tip: Usted acts like él and ella: está!

questions.explain: Usted uses the same verb form as él and ella: habla.
questions.tip: Usted borrows the he/she verb form: habla!

questions.q: In Latin America, what is the plural you for a group, formal or informal?
questions.explain: Latin America uses ustedes for all plural you. Vosotros is used mainly in Spain for informal plural.
questions.tip: Ustedes is the y'all of Latin America!

questions.explain: Siéntese is the usted command; siéntate is the tú command.
questions.tip: Formal commands flip the vowel: sentarse becomes siéntese!

questions.explain: Su is the possessive for usted (also his, her, their).
questions.tip: Su is the all-purpose your for usted!

questions.q: What is the common written abbreviation of usted?
questions.explain: Ud. (plural Uds.). Vd. is an older abbreviation.
questions.tip: Ud. is short and sweet!

questions.q: How do you politely get a stranger's attention?
questions.explain: Disculpe (or Perdone) means Excuse me to get attention.
questions.tip: Disculpe: no culpa (blame) on me - excuse me!

questions.q: ¿Podría ayudarme? sounds more polite than ¿Puede ayudarme?
questions.explain: True. The conditional (podría) softens a request, like could vs can in English.
questions.tip: Podría is could - a please built into the verb!

questions.q: When talking to usted, which object pronoun means you in Me alegra conocer___?
questions.explain: Usted takes lo or la as a direct object: Me alegra conocerlo / conocerla. Te is for tú.
questions.tip: Usted borrows lo and la, just like él and ella!

questions.explain: Embarazada means pregnant. Embarrassed is avergonzado or tener vergüenza.
questions.tip: Don't say estoy embarazada when you're embarrassed - unless you're expecting!

questions.explain: Éxito means success. An exit is una salida.
questions.tip: Éxito is success - the exit is la salida!

questions.explain: Ropa means clothes. Rope is una cuerda or una soga.
questions.tip: Ropa: you hang clothes on a rope (clothesline)!

questions.explain: Un pariente is any relative. Parents are los padres.
questions.tip: Parents are parientes, but so is your cousin!

questions.explain: Decepción means disappointment. Deception is engaño.
questions.tip: Decepción: disappointment, not deception!

questions.explain: Casualidad means chance or coincidence: ¡Qué casualidad! What a coincidence!
questions.tip: Casualidad: a casual coincidence!

questions.explain: Fábrica means factory. Fabric is tela.
questions.tip: A fábrica might make fabric, but it's the factory!

questions.explain: Largo means long. Large is grande.
questions.tip: In music, largo means slow and broad - it takes a long time!

questions.explain: Contestar means to answer or reply.
questions.tip: Contestar: answer the contest question!

questions.explain: Asistir a una reunión means to attend a meeting. To help is ayudar.
questions.tip: Asistir = attend; ayudar = help!

questions.explain: Tú with an accent is the pronoun you; tu without an accent means your.
questions.tip: Tú wears a hat because it's a person; tu just owns things!

questions.explain: Él with an accent means he; el without an accent means the.
questions.tip: Él wears a hat because he's a person!

questions.explain: Sí with an accent means yes; si without an accent means if.
questions.tip: Sí wears a hat because yes is confident!

questions.explain: Agua is feminine. It takes el only because it starts with a stressed a sound, so the adjective is fría.
questions.tip: El agua is a girl in disguise - el just avoids an a-a clash!

questions.explain: The personal a is used before a person who is the direct object: Veo a mi hermano.
questions.tip: Personal a: people get an a, things don't!

questions.q: What is the contraction of a + el?
questions.explain: A + el becomes al: Voy al mercado. De + el becomes del.
questions.tip: A + el squeeze together into al!

questions.q: Yo ___ a María. (to know a person)
questions.explain: Conocer is for people and places: conozco. Saber is for facts and skills.
questions.tip: Conocer is for people you've connected with!

questions.explain: Saber + infinitive means to know how to: Sé nadar.
questions.tip: Saber is for skills and facts: sé, I know!

questions.q: No veo nada is correct Spanish.
questions.explain: True. Spanish uses double negatives: No veo nada means I don't see anything.
questions.tip: Spanish negatives team up: no + nada!

questions.explain: Hay means there is or there are: Hay tres libros.
questions.tip: Hay sounds like 'eye' - I see there are three!
